# neuropile v0.1.3 - full documentation

> Complete documentation for the neuropile package, concatenated into a
> single file. This is the "llmsFull" target for agents that want everything
> in one read.

Package: npmjs.com/package/neuropile
Repository: git+https://github.com/Damian-Mostert/neuropile.git

---

# getting-started

# Getting started with neuropile

Everything you need to run a brain in under five minutes, then go deeper.

## Install

```bash
npm install neuropile
```

Node 18 or newer. That is the only hard requirement.

The package ships a C++17 addon. During `npm install` it tries to compile it
with `node-gyp`. If no compiler is available it prints a short notice and
installs a pure-JavaScript fallback instead. Both expose the identical API, so
your code never needs to care which one is running.

Check which one you got:

```js
const { nativeAvailable } = require('neuropile');
console.log(nativeAvailable); // true = C++ addon, false = JS fallback
```

### If the addon did not build

npm 12 blocks dependency install scripts by default, which includes the
`node-gyp` build. If `nativeAvailable` is `false`, approve the build script:

```bash
npm approve-scripts neuropile
npm rebuild neuropile
```

Or add it to your own `package.json`:

```json
{
  "allowScripts": {
    "neuropile": true
  }
}
```

## Your first brain

```js
const { Brain } = require('neuropile');

const brain = new Brain({ sizeGB: 0.1 });
```

That creates a brain with **154,000 neurons** spread across 16 regions. That
is a lot of neurons for a first script, and it takes a moment to wire up. For
anything you are iterating on, use a small brain:

```js
const brain = new Brain({ sizeGB: 0.01 }); // 15,024 neurons - fast to build
const brain = new Brain({ neurons: 5000 }); // explicit count
```

Sizing rules of thumb:

| Want | Use |
| --- | --- |
| A quick script or test | `{ neurons: 5000 }` or `{ sizeGB: 0.01 }` |
| A demo or small agent | `{ sizeGB: 0.05 }` |
| A full brain | `{ sizeGB: 0.1 }` (154,000 neurons) |

## The core loop

A brain is a simulation. You feed it input, you advance time, you read the
result.

```js
const brain = new Brain({ sizeGB: 0.01 });

// 1. Give it input
brain.hear('the room is cold and quiet');

// 2. Advance time
brain.tick(5);

// 3. Read the result
console.log(brain.emotionalState()); // { valence, arousal, drive, ... }
console.log(brain.behaviorState());  // { curiosity, uncertainty, ... }
```

`tick(n)` advances the simulation by n steps. Each step runs the spiking
engine, decays the needs, and updates the neuromodulators.

You do not have to call `tick()` manually. `brain.start(hz)` runs a timer that
ticks automatically:

```js
brain.start(10); // ticks at 10 Hz
// ... later
brain.stop();
```

Use manual `tick()` when you want deterministic, step-by-step control. Use
`start()` when the brain should run continuously alongside your app.

## Feeding it things

There are three ways to put information in.

### Words — `hear()`

```js
brain.hear('the fire is warm');
```

`hear()` splits the text into words, hashes each one into a sensory pattern,
drives the thalamus/sensory/amygdala, activates matching concepts, **and
stores the whole utterance as an episodic memory**.

That last part surprises people. If you do not want `hear()` to also remember,
pass `{ remember: false }`.

### Vectors — `perceive()` and `see()`

```js
brain.perceive([0.2, 0, 0.9]);              // dense sensory vector
brain.see(new Uint32Array([1, 2, 3, 500])); // sparse visual indices
```

`perceive()` auto-detects the format: a `Uint32Array`/`Int32Array` is
treated as sparse neuron indices, a plain array is treated as a dense
value vector. Pass `{ channel: 'visual' }` to route to the visual region.

### The world — `integrateWorldState()`

This is the richest input. It takes a snapshot of the world and drives the
appropriate regions.

```js
brain.integrateWorldState({
  body: { x: 0.5, y: 0.4, speed: 0.2 },
  needs: { hunger: 0.3, energy: 0.6, joy: 0.7 },
  detections: [{ label: 'food', w: 0.8 }],
  interaction: { note: 'feed', x: 0.5, y: 0.4 },
});
```

| Field | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `body` | Position, heading, speed. Drives spatial neurons and border alarm. |
| `needs` | `hunger`, `energy`, `joy` (0..1). Low needs become distress signals. |
| `detections` | `{ label, w }` objects. Labels are hashed into visual neurons. |
| `interaction` | `{ note }` — `feed`, `rest`, `poke`, `danger` are handled specially. |
| `opticFlow` | `{ x, y, magnitude }` — visual motion. |
| `motorHint` | `{ x, y, intensity }` — a suggested direction, used by `selfAwareness()`. |

## Memory

```js
// Store
brain.remember('the fire is warm and safe', {
  entities: ['fire', 'warm'],
  emotion: 'happy',
  salience: 0.5,
  type: 'episodic',
});

// Recall
const memories = brain.recall(['fire'], { topN: 5 });
console.log(brain.recallText(['fire'])); // human-readable
```

Memory types are `'episodic'`, `'semantic'`, `'procedural'`, and
`'utterance'`.

Recall is **biased by neural reafference**: memories whose encoding pattern
overlaps with the neurons currently firing come first. This is what makes the
simulation drive cognition rather than sit next to it. Pass `{ neural: false }`
to disable it and get purely semantic matching.

Memories do not decay on their own. Call `brain.forget()` to run a decay and
prune pass.

## Concepts

A concept is a label on an experienced cluster. It accumulates sensory
features and an emotional vector.

```js
brain.learn('ember', { bright: 0.9, hot: 0.8 }, { valence: 0.4, arousal: 0.3 }, 'watch', 0.6);
brain.associate('ember', 'fire', 0.4);

console.log(brain.emotionOf('ember')); // { valence, arousal, approach }
console.log(brain.activeConcepts(5));
```

The third argument is the emotional vector, the fourth is an action label,
and the fifth is the learning strength (0..1).

## Working memory

A small, fast-decaying attention buffer — 7 slots, 12 second lifetime.

```js
brain.hold('we are talking about fire', ['fire'], 'input');
brain.focus('fire', ['fire', 'warm'], 'input');

console.log(brain.readWorkingMemory());
console.log(brain.getFocus());
```

Source types have different priorities, so the right thing gets evicted
first: `input` (4) > `answer` (3) > `grounding` (2) > `thought` (1) >
`self_speech` (0).

Call `brain.rehearse(['fire'])` to keep items alive.

## Beliefs

Beliefs are explicit claims with provenance, kept separate from memories so a
generated sentence never silently becomes knowledge.

```js
brain.believe({ topic: 'fire', claim: 'fire is warm', confidence: 0.6 });
brain.believe({ topic: 'fire', claim: 'fire is warm', source: 'observation', verified: true });

console.log(brain.deliberate('fire'));
```

`deliberate()` returns `{ topic, evidenceCount, alternatives, concluded,
conclusion }`. It clusters agreeing claims and only concludes when there is
verified evidence or agreement from two or more independent sources.

## Reading the brain

### `brain.state()`

The full picture, as a plain object. Keys: `tick`, `native`, `neurons`,
`maxNeurons`, `growthProgress`, `growthEvents`, `emotion`, `behavior`,
`motorIntent`, `concepts`, `netEmotion`, `workingMemory`, `focus`,
`memorySize`, `conceptSize`, `beliefs`, `internal`.

### `brain.context()`

A compact text block built for an LLM prompt. This is the intended way to
give a language model the brain's state:

```js
const prompt = `You are a character with this inner state:\n\n${brain.context()}`;
```

It emits `NEURAL`, `AFFECT`, `BEHAVIOR`, `NEEDS`, `CONCEPTS`,
`WORKING MEMORY`, `MEMORIES`, and optionally `GENOME LEDGER` and
`METACOGNITION` lines.

### `brain.emotionalState()` / `brain.behaviorState()`

The affect numbers directly.

- `emotionalState()` → `{ valence, arousal, drive, norepinephrine, needs, body }`
- `behaviorState()` → `{ valence, arousal, drive, curiosity, uncertainty, actionReadiness, patience, speechReadiness, researchDrive }`

## Moving the brain

The core produces a motor intent, and you decide how to apply it.

```js
const intent = brain.getMotorIntent(); // { dx, dy, strength }
```

`dx`/`dy` are a normalized direction, `strength` is 0..1. This is the decoded
movement signal — use it to drive a character in a game, a robot, or a
simulated body.

`brain.move(dx, dy, intensity)` moves the brain's internal body and applies
the corresponding motor pulses.

## Saving and loading

```js
brain.save('./agent.neuropile');       // gzip-compressed by default
const clone = new Brain({ sizeGB: 0.01 });
clone.load('./agent.neuropile');

const snap = brain.snapshot();         // plain in-memory object
clone.restore(snap);
```

Async variants exist too: `await brain.saveAsync(path)` and
`await clone.loadAsync(path)`.

The loader auto-detects gzip by its magic bytes, so compressed and
uncompressed files are both readable regardless of how they were written.

## Growing a brain

```js
const brain = new Brain({
  startNeurons: 20000,
  maxNeurons: 200000,
  growthBatch: 1000,
  growthInterval: 100, // ticks between automatic growth events
});

brain.tick(100);       // one growth event fires
console.log(brain.neuronCount); // 20020
```

New neurons are wired into the circuit the same way the original brain was
wired, and everything already learned is preserved. Growth is automatic
whenever `maxNeurons` exceeds the starting size; set `autoGrow: false` for
manual control with `brain.grow(n)` and `brain.growTo(target)`.

Region sizes round to multiples of 1000, so `startNeurons: 20000` actually
starts at 19,020 neurons. See [gotchas](gotchas.md#growth-numbers-are-not-exact).

## Module exports

```js
const neuropile = require('neuropile');
```

| Export | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Brain` | class | High-level brain: the core plus every cognitive layer. |
| `BrainCore` | class | The JavaScript core implementation. |
| `NativeBrainCore` | class \| null | The native core, or `null` if the addon is unavailable. |
| `NeuralEngine` | class | The JavaScript spiking engine. |
| `NativeNeuralEngine` | class \| null | The native engine, or `null` if unavailable. |
| `MemoryCortex` | class | Associative memory. |
| `ConceptNet` | class | Word grounding. |
| `WorkingMemory` | class | Attention buffer. |
| `Genome` | class | Tunable parameters. |
| `Metacognition` | class | Self-prediction and self-scoring. |
| `Homeostasis` | class | Parameter trial-and-error. |
| `BeliefStore` | class | Explicit claims with provenance. |
| `createCore(options)` | function | Build a standalone core using the standard selection logic. |
| `soundPattern(text, size)` | function | Hash text into a sensory pattern of neuron indices. |
| `labelHash(label)` | function | Deterministic hash used for detection labels. |
| `persistence` | object | `save`, `load`, `saveAsync`, `loadAsync`, `encodeValue`, `decodeValue`, `toSerializable`, `fromSerializable`. |
| `save(brain, path, opts)` | function | Shortcut for `persistence.save`. |
| `load(brain, path)` | function | Shortcut for `persistence.load`. |
| `nativeAvailable` | boolean | Whether the native addon loaded successfully. |
| `nativeModule` | object \| null | The raw native module, or `null`. |
| `nativeError` | Error \| null | The error from the failed load, if any. |
| `nativePath` | string \| null | Resolved path of the loaded addon, or `null`. |
| `SENSORY_SIZE` | number | `400000` — default sensory region size. |
| `PATTERN_LENGTH` | number | `200` — indices per sensory pattern. |
| `VERSION` | string | The package version. |

ESM: `import { Brain } from 'neuropile';` — every named export above is
available.

---

## Constructor options

Accepted by `new Brain(options)` and `new BrainCore(options)`.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sizeGB` | `0.1` | Model size. `0.1` yields 154,000 neurons. `0.01` yields 15,024. |
| `neurons` | — | Explicit neuron count. Overrides `sizeGB` when greater than 0. |
| `startNeurons` | — | Initial size. Alias for `neurons` that reads as growth intent. |
| `maxNeurons` | start size | Hard ceiling on total neurons. Clamped up to the start size, never down. |
| `autoGrow` | `maxNeurons > start` | Grow automatically during `tick()`. |
| `growthBatch` | ~1% of start | Neurons added per growth event. |
| `growthInterval` | `100` | Ticks between automatic growth events. `0` disables the timer. |
| `growthFanout` | `8` | Synapses wired per direction for each new neuron. |
| `growthProfile` | object \| array | Per-region growth multipliers. Object is keyed by region name; array is positional. |
| `synapsesPerNeuron` | `200` | Synapse slots reserved per neuron. |
| `maxConnections` | `50000` | Maximum sampled connections per wiring rule. |
| `wire` | `true` | Wire the region graph at construction. |
| `seed` | — | Deterministic seed for the JavaScript fallback. Makes wiring reproducible. |
| `native` | `true` | Set `false` to force the JS core even when the addon is built. |
| `core` | — | Supply a pre-built core instead of constructing one. |
| `coreOptions` | — | Options forwarded to the core when using the `Brain` wrapper. |

---

## `Brain`

```js
const brain = new Brain({ sizeGB: 0.1 });
```

### Properties

All read-only getters.

| Property | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `engine` | `NeuralEngine` | The raw engine with the typed-array neuron state. |
| `regions` | `Region[]` | The 16 regions with `start`, `end`, `size`, `threshold`, `inhibRatio`. |
| `tickCount` | number | Ticks elapsed. |
| `valence` | number | Current emotional valence, roughly -1..1. |
| `arousal` | number | Current arousal. |
| `drive` | number | Current drive. |
| `needs` | object | `{ hunger, energy, joy }`, each 0..1. |
| `body` | object | `{ x, y, heading, speed, energy }`. |
| `motorState` | object | `{ moveX, moveY, lastAction }`. |
| `neuronCount` | number | Current neuron count. |
| `maxNeurons` | number | The growth ceiling. |
| `canGrow` | boolean | `false` once the ceiling is reached. |
| `growthProgress` | number | 0..1 toward the ceiling. |
| `growthEvents` | number | How many growth events have happened. |
| `native` | boolean | Whether the native core is in use. |
| `core` | `BrainCore` | The underlying core. |
| `genome` | `Genome` | The parameter genome. |
| `memory` | `MemoryCortex` | Associative memory. |
| `concepts` | `ConceptNet` | Concept store. |
| `workingMemory` | `WorkingMemory` | Attention buffer. |
| `metacognition` | `Metacognition` | Self-prediction log. |
| `homeostasis` | `Homeostasis` | Parameter trial ledger. |
| `beliefs` | `BeliefStore` | Explicit claims. |

### Clock

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tick(count = 1)` | number | Advance the simulation. Also advances working memory. Returns the new tick count. |
| `step(count = 1)` | number | Alias for `tick`. |
| `start(hz = 10)` | `this` | Start a timer that ticks automatically. The timer is `unref`'d, so it will not hold the process open. |
| `stop()` | `this` | Stop the automatic timer. |

### Perception

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `perceive(input, options = {})` | `EmotionalState` | Feed a stimulus. A string is treated as words (same as `hear`). A typed array is sparse indices; a plain array is a dense vector. |
| `hear(text, options = {})` | `EmotionalState` | Hash words into sensory patterns, activate concepts, and store the utterance as an episodic trace. |
| `see(input)` | `EmotionalState` | Perceive into the visual region. |

`perceive` options: `channel` (`'sensory'`, `'visual'`, `'audio'`),
`encode` (boolean, also encode into memory), `encodeStrength` (default `0.8`).

`hear` options: `strength` (default `1.0`), `remember` (default `true` — set
`false` to skip the automatic episodic trace), `entities`, `emotion`,
`salience` (default `0.45`), `encodeNeural` (default `true`).

### Memory

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `remember(content, options = {})` | `MemoryNode \| undefined` | Store a memory, encode it into the hippocampus, and ground its words as concepts. |
| `recall(entities = [], options = {})` | `MemoryNode[]` | Recall memories, biased by neural reafference. |
| `recallFact(keyword)` | `MemoryNode[]` | Recall semantic facts matching a keyword. |
| `recallText(entities = [], options = {})` | string | Recall and format as human-readable text. |
| `forget()` | `this` | Run a decay pass on memory and prune concepts. |

`remember` options: `entities` (string[]), `emotion` (default `'neutral'`),
`salience` (default `0.5`), `dopamine` (default `0`), `type` (default
`'semantic'`), `turnId` (default `null`), `encodeNeural` (default `true`),
`consolidate` (boolean), `consolidateStrength` (default `0.5`), `strength`
(default `0.7`), `concepts` (default `true`), `sensory`, `conceptEmotion`.

`recall` options: `emotion` (default `'neutral'`), `topN` (default `8`),
`context` (default `'conversation'`), `neural` (default `true` — set `false`
to disable reafference biasing), `reafferenceTopN` (default `20`).

`recall` also accepts a bare string as the first argument.

### Concepts

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `activate(word, strength = 1.0)` | concept \| null | Activate a concept by label. |
| `learn(word, sensory = {}, emotion = {}, action = null, strength = 0.5)` | concept \| null | Teach a word a sensory profile and emotional vector. Also grounds it in the neural substrate. |
| `associate(wordA, wordB, strength = 0.3)` | `EmotionVector \| null` | Link two concepts. |
| `emotionOf(word)` | `EmotionVector \| null` | `{ valence, arousal, approach }` for a word. |
| `activeConcepts(topN = 8)` | `ConceptSnapshot[]` | The most active concepts. |
| `netEmotion()` | `EmotionVector` | The combined emotion of all active concepts. |

### Working memory

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hold(content, entities = [], type = 'thought', strength = 1.0)` | `this` | Put something in attention. |
| `focus(topic, entities = [], source = 'thought', strength = 1.0)` | `Focus \| null` | Set the shared focus point. |
| `getFocus()` | `Focus \| null` | Read the focus. Expires after 12 seconds. |
| `readWorkingMemory(topN)` | `WorkingMemorySlot[]` | Read the slots, strongest first. |
| `rehearse(entities = [])` | `this` | Keep matching items alive. |

### Beliefs

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `believe(claim, options = {})` | `Belief \| null` | Record a claim. Also accepts a single object `{ topic, claim, source, confidence, verified }`. |
| `beliefsAbout(topic, limit = 3)` | `Belief[]` | Recall beliefs about a topic. |
| `deliberate(topic)` | `Deliberation` | Cluster evidence and report alternatives plus a conclusion. |

`Deliberation` is `{ topic, evidenceCount, alternatives, concluded, conclusion }`.

### Metacognition and homeostasis

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `predict(parsed = {}, reafStrength = 0)` | record | Predict the next internal state before responding. `parsed` is `{ intent, emotion }`. |
| `observe(record, responseText)` | number | Score the prediction against what happened. Returns a dopamine delta, applied to the core. |
| `recordTurn(metrics = {})` | string \| null | Record a turn. Evaluates homeostasis every 20 turns and returns a log line when it does. |
| `tune()` | string \| null | Force a homeostasis evaluation now. |

`recordTurn` metrics: `interrupted`, `recalledSalience`, `goalPushed`,
`goalResolved`.

### Growth

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `grow(count)` | number | Add up to `count` neurons. Capped by `maxNeurons`. Returns how many were added. |
| `growTo(target)` | number | Grow toward a total neuron count. Returns how many were added. |
| `maybeGrow()` | number | Apply one automatic growth step if the cadence allows it. |

### Readout

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `emotionalState()` | `EmotionalState` | `{ valence, arousal, drive, norepinephrine, needs, body }`. |
| `behaviorState()` | `BehaviorState` | `{ valence, arousal, drive, curiosity, uncertainty, actionReadiness, patience, speechReadiness, researchDrive }`. |
| `motorIntent()` | `MotorIntent` | `{ dx, dy, strength }` — the decoded movement signal. |
| `state()` | object | Everything, as one plain object. |
| `context()` | string | A compact, model-ready text block. |

### Persistence

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `snapshot()` | object | A plain in-memory snapshot. |
| `restore(snapshot)` | `this` | Restore from a snapshot. |
| `save(filePath, options)` | string | Write a gzip-compressed snapshot. Returns the resolved path. |
| `load(filePath)` | object | Load a snapshot and apply it. Returns the snapshot. |
| `saveAsync(filePath, options)` | `Promise<string>` | Async save. |
| `loadAsync(filePath)` | `Promise<object>` | Async load. |

`save` options: `compress` (default `true` — set `false` for plain JSON).

### Core passthrough

These are proxied straight to `brain.core`, so they work identically on the
native and JS cores.

| Method | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `reward(strength = 1.0)` | number — the new dopamine level. |
| `punish(strength = 1.0)` | number — the new dopamine level. |
| `setNeeds(needs)` | `Needs` |
| `getNeeds()` | `Needs` |
| `getBody()` | `Body` |
| `getMotorState()` | `MotorState` |
| `move(dx = 0, dy = 0, intensity = 1.0)` | `Body` |
| `integrateWorldState(state = {})` | `EmotionalState` |
| `handleInteraction(kind, intensity = 1.0)` | `Needs` |
| `amygdalaActivate(threatLevel = 0.5)` | number |
| `startle(strength = 1.0)` | void |
| `decideBehavior(options = {})` | `BehaviorDecision` |
| `actionSelection()` | void |
| `novelty()` | number |
| `reafference(topN = 20)` | `{ indices, strength }` |
| `selfAwareness()` | number |
| `getMotorIntent()` | `MotorIntent` |
| `readInternalState()` | `Record<string, number>` — `Ω1`..`Ω5`, `Ω_acc`, `Ω_bg`, `Ω_hypo`, `Ω_da`, `Ω_ne`. |
| `neuronMap()` | `Record<string, { mean, peak, firing }>` — one entry per region. |
| `thought()` | `Float32Array` — the association region's activation. |
| `perceiveDense(values)` | void |
| `perceiveVisual(input)` | void |
| `hearDense(values)` | void |
| `encode(input, strength = 1.0)` | void — encodes into the hippocampus. |
| `encodeDense(values, strength = 1.0)` | void |
| `consolidate(input, strength = 1.0)` | void — encodes into the temporal cortex. |
| `consolidateDense(values, strength = 1.0)` | void |
| `motorQuadrantSize()` | number |
| `region(name)` | `Region \| null` |

---

## `BrainCore`

The spiking substrate on its own, without the cognitive layers. Use it when
you want raw neural dynamics.

```js
const { BrainCore } = require('neuropile');
const core = new BrainCore({ neurons: 50000, seed: 42 });
```

It has every method in [Core passthrough](#core-passthrough) plus:

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tick(count = 1)` | number | Advance the simulation. |
| `start(hz = 10)` / `stop()` | `this` | Automatic ticking. |
| `snapshot()` / `restore(snapshot)` | object / `this` | Persistence. |
| `grow` / `growTo` / `maybeGrow` | number | Neurogenesis. |
| `perceive` / `perceiveDense` / `perceiveVisual` / `hear` / `hearDense` | void | Raw input. |
| `encode` / `encodeDense` / `consolidate` / `consolidateDense` | void | Raw memory encoding. |

Properties: `engine`, `regions`, `options`, `tickCount`, `valence`, `arousal`,
`drive`, `needs`, `body`, `motorState`, `neuronCount`, `maxNeurons`,
`canGrow`, `growthProgress`, `growthEvents`.

### `decideBehavior(options)`

```js
core.decideBehavior({
  activeGoal: { urgency: 0.8 },
  humanPresent: true,
  pendingSelfSpeech: true,
  tickCount: 120,
  lastSpokeTick: 0,
});
```

Returns the behavior state plus `canSpeak`, `shouldResearch`, `shouldAct`,
and `responseMode` (`'grounded'`, `'speak'`, or `'quiet'`).

### `integrateWorldState(state)`

| Field | Type | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `body` | `{ x, y, heading, speed, vx, vy }` | Spatial neurons, border alarm, motion signal. |
| `needs` | `{ hunger, energy, joy }` | Drive signals; low needs trigger distress and pain. |
| `detections` | `[{ label, w }]` | Labels are hashed into visual neurons. Salient labels (`self`, `violet-glow`, `cyan-light`, `warm-glow`) also reward. |
| `interaction` | `{ note, x, y, hungerLevel }` | `feed`, `poke`, `aversive`, `danger`, and `food` notes get special handling. |
| `opticFlow` | `{ x, y, magnitude }` | Visual motion into the visual quadrant system. |
| `motorHint` | `{ x, y, intensity, hintMode }` | A suggested direction, consumed by `selfAwareness()`. |

### `handleInteraction(kind, intensity = 1.0)`

Recognised kinds: `feed`, `rest`, `play`, `poke`, `danger`. Anything else is
treated as mildly aversive.

---

## Cognitive layer classes

Each layer can be used standalone.

### `MemoryCortex`

```js
const { MemoryCortex, Genome } = require('neuropile');
const memory = new MemoryCortex(new Genome());
```

| Method | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `encode(content, entities, emotion, salience, dopamine, type, turnId)` | `MemoryNode \| undefined` |
| `recall(entities, emotion, topN, context)` | `MemoryNode[]` |
| `recallByReafference(neuralIndices, entities, emotion, topN, context)` | `MemoryNode[]` |
| `recallFact(keyword)` | `MemoryNode[]` |
| `format(memories)` | string |
| `decay()` | void |
| `snapshot()` / `restore(snapshot)` | object / `this` |

Property: `size` (node count), `nodes` (the array).

### `ConceptNet`

| Method | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `activate(word, strength, hopDepth)` | concept \| null |
| `learn(word, sensory, emotion, action, strength)` | concept \| null |
| `associate(wordA, wordB, strength)` | void |
| `emotionOf(word)` | `EmotionVector \| null` |
| `activeConceptsSnapshot(topN)` | `ConceptSnapshot[]` |
| `formatForLLM()` | string \| null |
| `netEmotion()` | `EmotionVector` |
| `prune()` | void |

### `WorkingMemory`

| Method | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `hold(content, entities, type, strength)` | void |
| `setFocus(topic, entities, source, strength)` | `Focus \| null` |
| `getFocus()` / `clearFocus()` | `Focus \| null` / void |
| `rehearse(entities)` | void |
| `tick()` | void — expires old slots. |
| `read(topN)` | `WorkingMemorySlot[]` |
| `format()` | string |
| `flush()` | void |

### `Genome`

| Method | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `get(key)` | number \| null |
| `set(key, value)` | boolean — false if the key is unknown. Clamps to bounds. |
| `meta(key)` | `{ value, min, max, step } \| null` |
| `snapshot()` / `restore(snapshot)` | `Record<string, number>` / void |
| `keys()` | string[] |

Parameters: `metacognition_lr`, `emotion_cue`, `novelty_cue`, `arousal_cue`,
`drive_cue`, `salience_emotion_bonus`, `salience_entity_weight`,
`ne_interrupt_threshold`, `memory_decay_rate`, `memory_consolidate_boost`,
`memory_prune_threshold`.

### `Metacognition`

| Method | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `predict(neuralState, parsed, reafStrength)` | record |
| `observe(record, neuralStateAfter, responseText)` | number — dopamine delta |
| `recentAccuracy()` | number \| null |
| `summary()` | `MetacognitionSummary \| null` |

### `Homeostasis`

| Method | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `recordTurn(metrics)` | void |
| `evaluate()` | string \| null — a log line describing the trial. |
| `ledgerSummary(n)` | string \| null |

Property: `ledger` — an array of trial records.

### `BeliefStore`

| Method | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `record({ topic, claim, source, confidence, verified })` | `Belief \| null` |
| `recall(topic, limit)` | `Belief[]` |
| `best(topic)` | `Belief \| null` |
| `deliberate(topic)` | `Deliberation` |

Property: `items` — the array of beliefs.

---

## Utilities

### `createCore(options)`

Builds a standalone `BrainCore`, choosing the native or JS implementation
with the same logic `Brain` uses.

```js
const { createCore } = require('neuropile');
const core = createCore({ startNeurons: 50000, native: false });
```

### `soundPattern(text, size = 400000)`

Hashes text into a `Uint32Array` of 200 neuron indices. A djb2 hash
(`h = 5381`, `h = h * 31 ^ charCode`) spread with
`(h ^ j) * 2654435761 % size`. Results are cached, so repeated words are free.

### `labelHash(label)`

A deterministic 32-bit hash of a lowercase label. Used to place detection
labels into the visual region consistently.

### `persistence`

```js
const { persistence } = require('neuropile');

persistence.save(brain, './agent.neuropile');
persistence.save(brain, './agent.json', { compress: false });
const snapshot = persistence.load(brain, './agent.neuropile');
```

Async variants, inside an async function:

```js
await persistence.saveAsync(brain, './agent.neuropile');
await persistence.loadAsync(brain, './agent.neuropile');
```

`encodeValue` and `decodeValue` preserve typed arrays, `Map`, `Set`, and
`BigInt` through JSON. `toSerializable` and `fromSerializable` wrap a
snapshot in the on-disk envelope.

---

## Types

Full TypeScript definitions are bundled in `index.d.ts` and are picked up
automatically.

```ts
import { Brain, BrainOptions, EmotionalState, BehaviorState } from 'neuropile';

const options: BrainOptions = { sizeGB: 0.05, maxNeurons: 200000 };
const brain = new Brain(options);
const emotion: EmotionalState = brain.emotionalState();
```

# Patterns

## Give a language model the brain's state

The core integration. `brain.context()` returns a compact text block built to
sit in a prompt.

```js
const { Brain } = require('neuropile');

const brain = new Brain({ sizeGB: 0.05 });

async function respond(userText, llm) {
  brain.hear(userText);
  brain.hold(userText, userText.toLowerCase().split(/\s+/), 'input');
  brain.focus(userText, userText.toLowerCase().split(/\s+/), 'input');
  brain.tick(2);

  const context = brain.context();
  const reply = await llm({
    system: `You are a character with an inner life. Here is your state:\n\n${context}`,
    user: userText,
  });

  // Let the brain react to what was said back to it.
  const record = brain.predict({ intent: 'response', emotion: 'neutral' }, 0.5);
  brain.observe(record, reply);
  brain.recordTurn({ recalledSalience: 0.4 });

  return reply;
}
```

`context()` emits these lines:

```
NEURAL tick=5 native=true neurons=154000/154000
AFFECT valence=0.123 arousal=0.074 drive=0.029 ne=0.000
BEHAVIOR curiosity=0.37 uncertainty=0.28 action=0.04 speech=0.04
NEEDS hunger=0.50 energy=0.50 joy=0.50
CONCEPTS warm:0.68 friend:0.53
WORKING MEMORY
[thought] we are talking about fire
MEMORIES
(nothing relevant recalled)
```

Two optional lines appear when there is data: `GENOME LEDGER` (recent
homeostasis trials) and `METACOGNITION` (recent prediction accuracy).

---

## A chat character with memory

The key is that recall is biased by what the brain is currently thinking about,
so it remembers the relevant thing without you doing any retrieval work.

```js
const { Brain } = require('neuropile');

const brain = new Brain({ sizeGB: 0.05 });
brain.start(10); // ticks at 10 Hz in the background

function chat(userText) {
  brain.hear(userText, { salience: 0.6 });
  brain.hold(userText, userText.toLowerCase().split(/\s+/), 'input');
  brain.focus(userText, userText.toLowerCase().split(/\s+/), 'input');

  const memories = brain.recall(['topic'], { topN: 5 });
  const concepts = brain.activeConcepts(5);
  const emotion = brain.emotionalState();

  return { memories, concepts, emotion };
}
```

Note `brain.hear()` already stores the utterance as an episodic memory, so
you do not need a separate `remember()` call for conversation.

---

## A game agent that acts on its own

The brain produces a motor intent. You decide what to do with it.

```js
const { Brain } = require('neuropile');

const brain = new Brain({ sizeGB: 0.01 });

let body = { x: 0.5, y: 0.5, heading: 0, speed: 0 };
let food = { x: 0.3, y: 0.4 };

function step() {
  // Tell the brain what it perceives.
  brain.integrateWorldState({
    body,
    needs: brain.getNeeds(),
    detections: [{ label: 'food', w: 1 - Math.hypot(body.x - food.x, body.y - food.y) }],
  });

  // Read the brain's intent.
  const intent = brain.getMotorIntent();

  // Apply it (with a little steering so it does not get stuck).
  const dx = intent.dx * intent.strength + (food.x - body.x) * 0.12;
  const dy = intent.dy * intent.strength + (food.y - body.y) * 0.12;
  const mag = Math.hypot(dx, dy) || 1;

  brain.move(dx / mag, dy / mag, 0.7);
  body = brain.getBody();

  if (Math.hypot(body.x - food.x, body.y - food.y) < 0.05) {
    brain.handleInteraction('feed', 1.0);
    food = { x: Math.random(), y: Math.random() };
  }

  brain.tick(1);
}
```

`handleInteraction('feed')` raises hunger satisfaction and rewards the brain,
which is what makes the association between food and good outcomes form.

Recognised interaction kinds: `feed`, `rest`, `play`, `poke`, `danger`.

---

## An HTTP service over a brain

```js
const http = require('node:http');
const { Brain } = require('neuropile');

const brain = new Brain({ sizeGB: 0.01 });
brain.start(10);

const server = http.createServer(async (req, res) => {
  const chunks = [];
  for await (const chunk of req) chunks.push(chunk);
  const body = chunks.length ? JSON.parse(Buffer.concat(chunks)) : {};

  const send = (data) => {
    const payload = JSON.stringify(data);
    res.writeHead(200, { 'content-type': 'application/json' });
    res.end(payload);
  };

  if (req.url === '/state') return send(brain.state());
  if (req.url === '/context') return send({ context: brain.context() });

  if (req.url === '/perceive') {
    brain.hear(body.text || '');
    brain.tick(2);
    return send({ emotion: brain.emotionalState(), concepts: brain.activeConcepts(6) });
  }

  if (req.url === '/recall') {
    const memories = brain.recall(body.entities || [], { topN: 8 });
    return send({ memories });
  }

  send({ error: 'not found' });
});

server.listen(8787);
```

A fuller version is in `examples/http-server.js`, with routes for `/state`,
`/context`, `/perceive`, `/remember`, `/recall`, `/learn`, `/believe`,
`/step`, `/interact`, and `/save`.

---

## A character that learns words

```js
// Teach a word a sensory profile and how it feels.
brain.learn('ember', { bright: 0.9, hot: 0.8 }, { valence: 0.4, arousal: 0.3 }, 'watch', 0.6);

// Link it to another word.
brain.associate('ember', 'fire', 0.4);

// Later, ask how it feels.
brain.emotionOf('ember');   // { valence, arousal, approach }
brain.activeConcepts(5);   // the most active concepts
brain.netEmotion();         // combined emotion of active concepts
```

The `learn()` arguments are: word, sensory features, emotion vector, action
label, and strength. `learn()` also grounds the word in the neural substrate,
so it is not only a table lookup.

---

## A character with opinions

Beliefs are separate from memories on purpose, so a generated sentence never
quietly becomes knowledge.

```js
// Record a claim.
brain.believe({ topic: 'fire', claim: 'fire is warm', confidence: 0.6 });

// Record the same claim from an observation, and mark it verified.
brain.believe({ topic: 'fire', claim: 'fire is warm', source: 'observation', verified: true });

// Ask what the brain thinks.
const verdict = brain.deliberate('fire');
// {
//   topic: 'fire',
//   evidenceCount: 2,
//   alternatives: [{ claim: 'fire is warm', sources: ['observation','internal'], confidence: 0.425, verified: true }],
//   concluded: true,
//   conclusion: { claim: 'fire is warm', verified: true, sources: ['observation','internal'] }
// }
```

A conclusion requires verified evidence, or agreement from two or more
independent sources. One unverified claim is not enough.

`brain.beliefsAbout('fire')` returns the raw belief list.

---

## Growing a brain over time

```js
const brain = new Brain({
  startNeurons: 20000,
  maxNeurons: 200000,
  growthBatch: 1000,
  growthInterval: 100, // ticks between automatic growth events
  growthProfile: {
    hippocampus: 4, // grow memory capacity faster
    association: 3,
    motor: 0.2, // barely grow the motor system
  },
});

brain.tick(100); // one growth event fires
brain.neuronCount; // 20020
```

Manual control:

```js
brain.grow(500);        // add up to 500 neurons
brain.growTo(50000);    // grow toward a total
brain.maybeGrow();      // one automatic step, if the cadence allows
brain.canGrow;          // false at the ceiling
brain.growthProgress;   // 0..1
```

Everything already learned survives growth — the brain is remapped, not
rebuilt.

---

## Persistent agents

```js
// Save.
const path = brain.save('./agent.neuropile');

// Load into a fresh brain.
const restored = new Brain({ startNeurons: 20000, maxNeurons: 200000 });
restored.load('./agent.neuropile');
restored.neuronCount; // the grown size, not the starting size
```

The snapshot includes the neural engine, needs, body, memory, concepts,
working memory, genome, metacognition, beliefs, and the homeostasis ledger.

Plain JSON instead of gzip:

```js
brain.save('./agent.json', { compress: false });
```

Async versions: `await brain.saveAsync(path)` and `await restored.loadAsync(path)`.

---

## Embedding in an existing app

Use the core directly if you want the substrate without the cognitive layers.

```js
const { BrainCore } = require('neuropile');

const core = new BrainCore({ neurons: 50000, seed: 42 });

core.integrateWorldState({ body: { x: 0.5, y: 0.4 }, needs: { hunger: 0.3 } });
core.tick(10);

core.emotionalState();
core.getMotorIntent(); // { dx, dy, strength }
core.readInternalState(); // Ω1..Ω5, Ω_da, Ω_ne
```

Use `createCore(options)` to get the same core the `Brain` wrapper would have
built, including the native/JS selection logic.

---

## Testing

Use a small brain and a fixed seed. The JS fallback is deterministic with a
seed.

```js
const { Brain } = require('neuropile');

const brain = new Brain({ neurons: 2000, seed: 42, native: false });

brain.remember('the fire is warm', { entities: ['fire'] });
brain.tick(5);

assert.equal(brain.memory.size, 1);
assert.ok(brain.recall(['fire']).length > 0);
```

Use `{ native: false }` when you want to test the JavaScript path
specifically. The test suite in this repo runs every behaviour against both
implementations and asserts they agree.

For fast tests, `neurons: 2000` is enough. For a realistic feel, `sizeGB:
0.01`.

---

# gotchas

# Gotchas

The behaviours that surprise people. Read this before debugging something that
"should" have worked.

- [Growth numbers are not exact](#growth-numbers-are-not-exact)
- [`hear()` also remembers](#hear-also-remembers)
- [Memories do not decay on their own](#memories-do-not-decay-on-their-own)
- [`recall()` prefers what is firing right now](#recall-prefers-what-is-firing-right-now)
- [`believe()` takes two different shapes](#believe-takes-two-different-shapes)
- [The native addon may not have built](#the-native-addon-may-not-have-built)
- [`context()` is data, not prose](#context-is-data-not-prose)
- [Working memory is only seven slots](#working-memory-is-only-seven-slots)
- [Calls have side effects on needs](#calls-have-side-effects-on-needs)
- [Growth reallocates the whole engine](#growth-reallocates-the-whole-engine)
- [The brain is stochastic without a seed](#the-brain-is-stochastic-without-a-seed)
- [Typing is a string, not a number](#typing-is-a-string-not-a-number)

---

## Growth numbers are not exact

Region sizes are rounded to multiples of 1000, so the real neuron count is
never exactly what you asked for.

```js
const brain = new Brain({ startNeurons: 20000, maxNeurons: 200000 });
brain.neuronCount; // 19020, not 20000
```

The default `growthBatch` is ~1% of the **actual** start, so:

```js
const brain = new Brain({ startNeurons: 20000, maxNeurons: 200000 });
brain.tick(100);
brain.neuronCount; // 19210 (19020 + 190), not 20020
```

To land on an exact number, set `growthBatch` explicitly:

```js
const brain = new Brain({
  startNeurons: 20000,
  maxNeurons: 200000,
  growthBatch: 1000,
});
brain.tick(100);
brain.neuronCount; // 20020
```

Likewise `sizeGB: 0.1` gives 154,000 neurons and `sizeGB: 0.01` gives 15,024.
Neither is a round number.

**Do not assert exact neuron counts** unless you have set `growthBatch`
explicitly. Assert ranges, or compare relative growth.

---

## `hear()` also remembers

`hear()` is not just input. It hashes the words into sensory patterns,
activates matching concepts, **and stores the whole utterance as an episodic
memory**.

```js
brain.hear('hello');
brain.memory.size; // 1
```

If you want input without the memory side effect:

```js
brain.hear('hello', { remember: false });
```

This matters if you are counting memories, or if the user utterance should
not become a memory the character can later recall out of context.

---

## Memories do not decay on their own

Nothing decays until you call `forget()`.

```js
brain.remember('something', { entities: ['x'] });
brain.tick(1000);
brain.memory.size; // still 1 — no decay happened
```

Decay and pruning happen in `brain.forget()`:

```js
brain.forget();       // decays memory and prunes concepts
```

`forget()` is a single pass, so call it on a schedule if you want continuous
decay:

```js
setInterval(() => brain.forget(), 60_000);
```

Memory types decay at different rates: episodic fastest, semantic slowest.
Utterances decay very slowly.

---

## `recall()` prefers what is firing right now

Recall is biased by neural reafference — the neurons currently firing push
matching memories to the front. This is deliberate, and it is the main reason
the simulation drives cognition.

The consequence: **the same query can return different results depending on
the brain's internal state.**

```js
brain.remember('the fire is warm', { entities: ['fire'] });
brain.recall(['fire']); // may be empty if nothing neural matches
```

If you need deterministic semantic matching:

```js
brain.recall(['fire'], { neural: false });
```

Note that `recall([])` with no entities returns nothing. Use
`{ topN: 5 }` with an empty query only if you want the reafference-only
selection, which is what `brain.context()` does internally.

---

## `believe()` takes two different shapes

The method accepts a claim string or a full object.

```js
// String form - the topic must come from options.
brain.believe('fire is warm', { topic: 'fire', confidence: 0.6 });

// Object form - everything inline.
brain.believe({ topic: 'fire', claim: 'fire is warm', confidence: 0.6 });
```

The string form with no `topic` returns `null` and records nothing.

Two independent sources agreeing on the same claim are treated as evidence,
not a duplicate. Recording the same claim twice from the same source raises
confidence instead of adding a second entry.

---

## The native addon may not have built

```js
const { nativeAvailable } = require('neuropile');
nativeAvailable; // false means the JS fallback is in use
```

This is not an error — the JS fallback has the same API. But it is roughly
10x slower under heavy load, and it is the first thing to check if the brain
feels sluggish.

Common causes:

- No C++17 compiler installed.
- npm 12 blocking install scripts by default.

```bash
npm approve-scripts neuropile
npm rebuild neuropile
```

`require('neuropile').nativeError` holds the actual load error if you need
it.

---

## `context()` is data, not prose

`brain.context()` returns structured lines meant to be parsed and embedded.
It is not a paragraph and it does not address the user.

```
AFFECT valence=0.123 arousal=0.074 drive=0.029 ne=0.000
```

If you want natural language, generate it. Feed `context()` to a model and
ask it to describe the character's feelings in character.

Do not concatenate `context()` directly into a prompt without a delimiter
between it and the user's input, or the model may blur the two together.

---

## Working memory is only seven slots

Capacity is 7, hard-coded. Anything past that evicts the weakest slot.

```js
for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) brain.hold(`item ${i}`, [`e${i}`], 'thought');
brain.workingMemory.size; // 7
```

Eviction is by source priority first, then by strength:

| Source | Priority |
| --- | --- |
| `input` | 4 |
| `answer` | 3 |
| `grounding` | 2 |
| `thought` | 1 |
| `self_speech` | 0 |

Slots expire after 12 seconds of wall-clock time, not ticks. `rehearse()`
extends them.

---

## Calls have side effects on needs

Reading state is not always free of side effects.

`brain.emotionalState()` calls `_tickNeeds()` internally, which decays
hunger, energy, and joy. `brain.behaviorState()` calls `emotionalState()`, so
it does too.

If you poll `emotionalState()` in a tight loop, the brain will get hungry
much faster than if you only tick it occasionally.

Similarly, `brain.move()` consumes energy and reduces joy. `brain.tick(n)`
decays needs n times.

If you want a stable read, use `brain.valence` / `brain.arousal` /
`brain.drive` — those are plain getters with no side effects.

---

## Growth reallocates the whole engine

Growth is not incremental. It builds a new engine, remaps every neuron and
synapse into it, and swaps it in.

```js
const brain = new Brain({ startNeurons: 20000, maxNeurons: 200000 });
brain.tick(100); // one growth event — full reallocation
```

It is cheap at small sizes but not free. For a large brain, prefer fewer,
bigger growth events:

```js
{ growthBatch: 5000, growthInterval: 100 }
```

over many small ones.

Learned state is preserved: potentials, thresholds, and synapse weights all
survive the remap.

---

## The brain is stochastic without a seed

Wiring, growth distribution, and concept activation all use randomness.

```js
const a = new Brain({ startNeurons: 5000, native: false });
const b = new Brain({ startNeurons: 5000, native: false });
// different wiring, different results
```

For reproducible behaviour, set a seed:

```js
const brain = new Brain({ startNeurons: 5000, seed: 42, native: false });
```

The seed applies to the JavaScript fallback. The native core uses its own
generator, so only use seeds when you have forced `native: false` and are
testing the JS path.

---

## Typing is a string, not a number

Memory types are strings.

```js
brain.remember('x', { type: 'episodic' });   // correct
brain.remember('x', { type: 3 });             // wrong — not a valid type
```

Valid values are `'episodic'`, `'semantic'`, `'procedural'`, and
`'utterance'`.

The same applies to emotion names, working memory source types, and belief
sources — they are all free-form strings, but some are checked for special
behaviour:

- **Emotion**: `'neutral'`, `'happy'`, `'upset'` are read by the
  metacognitive predictor. Other strings are treated as neutral.
- **Interaction kind**: `'feed'`, `'rest'`, `'play'`, `'poke'`, `'danger'`
  have specific effects. Anything else is mildly aversive.
- **Belief source**: any string. `'observation'` and `'internal'` are
  conventions.

---

## Other things worth knowing

- **`brain.tick()` also advances working memory**, so slots expire on the
  same clock as the neurons.
- **`start()` timers are `unref`'d**, so they will not keep your process
  alive. Call `stop()` when you are done anyway.
- **`brain.core.engine`** gives you the raw typed arrays. On the native core
  these point directly at C++ memory and stay valid while the core is alive.
- **`soundPattern()` caches by text**, so hashing the same word repeatedly is
  free.
- **`maxNeurons` is clamped up** to the starting size, never down. Setting
  `maxNeurons` below the start size does not shrink the brain.

---

# Concepts

## The shape of the system

```
sensory / vision / audio
        │
        ▼
  BrainCore (C++ or JS)  ── spiking neurons, 16 regions, dopamine/NE
        │
        ├── emotionalState / behaviorState / motorIntent
        │
        ├── MemoryCortex      associative, decaying, reafference-biased
        ├── ConceptNet        sensory + emotional grounding of words
        ├── WorkingMemory     7 attention slots + shared focus
        ├── Genome            tunable personality/plasticity parameters
        ├── Metacognition     predicts, scores, adapts its own weights
        ├── Homeostasis       proposes genome trials, accepts or reverts
        └── BeliefStore       explicit claims with provenance
```

Two things are worth noticing.

**The split is deliberate.** Everything below `BrainCore` is pure JavaScript.
You can replace or extend the cognitive layers without recompiling the
native addon.

**The arrow goes both ways.** The core does not just sit under the cognitive
layers — the cognitive layers read back from it. `MemoryCortex.recall()` is
biased by `core.reafference()`, and `Metacognition` writes its error signal
back as dopamine through `core.reward()` / `core.punish()`. That feedback
loop is what makes this a brain rather than a database with a mood.

---

## The spiking engine

Neurons are leaky integrate-and-fire units.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Membrane potential | `Float32Array`, one per neuron |
| Decay | `0.95` per tick, times a per-neuron `decayRate` |
| Threshold | Per region, 0.08 to 0.35 |
| Inhibitory fraction | Per region, 5% to 35% — the first N% of each region |
| Refractory period | 20 ms |
| Hebbian rate | 0.012 |
| Weight decay | 0.002 |
| Weight bounds | -1.5 to 1.5 |
| Dopamine decay | 0.96 per tick |
| Norepinephrine decay | 0.92 per tick |

**Sparse decay** is the key performance trick. Only neurons that have actually
received input are updated on a tick, tracked in an active list. An idle
brain costs almost nothing, which is why a mostly-quiet brain is not
compute-bound.

**Firing** works like this: a neuron whose potential reaches its threshold
fires, resets to zero, and propagates to its synapse targets. Inhibitory
neurons propagate a negative weight. Firing is gated by the refractory
period, so a neuron cannot fire twice within 20 ms.

**Learning is dopamine-gated.** Hebbian strengthening only happens when
dopamine is outside the ±0.05 band. Otherwise synapses decay.

```js
brain.reward(0.5);   // dopamine up -> synapses strengthen
brain.punish(0.5);   // dopamine down -> synapses weaken
```

This is why reward and punishment change *what the brain learns*, not just
how it feels.

---

## The 16 regions

Regions are allocated proportionally to a fixed base size, so the brain keeps
its shape as it changes size.

| Region | Base size | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `thalamus` | 80,000 | Relay and gating. Carries body, need, and motion signals. |
| `hypothalamus` | 50,000 | Drives. Converts need pressure into arousal and drive. |
| `amygdala` | 40,000 | Valence and threat. Fires on aversive input. |
| `sensory` | 400,000 | Somatosensory and auditory channel. |
| `visual` | 100,000 | Visual channel, also used for object detections. |
| `hippocampus` | 160,000 | Memory encoding target. |
| `temporal` | 200,000 | Consolidation target — long-term storage. |
| `association` | 600,000 | Integration, concept grounding, reafference readout. |
| `prefrontal` | 300,000 | Inhibition, deliberation, self-awareness. |
| `acc` | 120,000 | Conflict detection. Feeds uncertainty. |
| `basalGanglia` | 180,000 | Action selection and motor gating. |
| `motor` | 240,000 | Movement output, in four directional quadrants. |
| `cerebellum` | 300,000 | Motor refinement and coordination. |
| `vta` | 20,000 | Dopamine source. |
| `locusCoeruleus` | 15,000 | Norepinephrine source. |
| `raphe` | 15,000 | Serotonin / stability source. |

At `sizeGB: 0.1` the scale factor is `0.1 / 1.82`, giving 154,000 neurons
total.

Read a region at runtime:

```js
const assoc = brain.core.region('association');
assoc.start;      // first neuron index
assoc.end;        // last neuron index
assoc.size;       // neuron count
assoc.threshold;  // firing threshold
assoc.inhibRatio; // inhibitory fraction
```

---

## Wiring

There is a wiring table of long-range projections between regions. Each entry
has a density, a minimum weight, and a maximum weight.

```js
['association', 'hippocampus', 0.7, 0.4, 0.9]
//  from           to            density  wMin  wMax
```

At construction, each rule samples `density × source region size` connections
(capped by `maxConnections`) and gives each a random weight in range.

Within each region, neurons are also wired to each other, so regions are not
isolated islands.

`maxConnections` (default 50,000) bounds the samples per rule. Lower it to
build a brain faster, or raise it for a denser connectome.

---

## Affect

Three numbers, all roughly in -1..1, all smoothed over time.

### Valence

How good or bad things feel. Driven by dopamine, minus need pressure, plus
serotonin stability, minus conflict penalty.

```js
brain.valence; // -1 (miserable) to 1 (delighted)
```

### Arousal

How activated the brain is. Driven by sensory and association activity, plus
hypothalamic pressure.

```js
brain.arousal; // 0 (calm) to 1 (highly activated)
```

### Drive

How much the brain wants to act. Driven by hippocampal activity and
hypothalamic pressure.

```js
brain.drive;
```

### Norepinephrine

The alerting signal. It rises when the amygdala detects a threat, and it
raises thresholds across the sensory and association regions — making the
brain more sensitive.

```js
brain.emotionalState().norepinephrine;
```

### Behavior state

Derived from the three affect numbers plus regional activity.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `curiosity` | Driven by hypothalamic pressure and novelty. |
| `uncertainty` | Driven by conflict detection in the ACC. |
| `actionReadiness` | Driven by basal ganglia and VTA. |
| `patience` | Driven by raphe stability and low arousal. |
| `speechReadiness` | Whether the brain wants to talk. |
| `researchDrive` | A blend of curiosity, uncertainty, and pressure. |

`decideBehavior()` combines these into `canSpeak`, `shouldResearch`,
`shouldAct`, and a `responseMode` of `'grounded'`, `'speak'`, or `'quiet'`.

---

## Needs and the body

Three needs, each 0..1: `hunger`, `energy`, `joy`.

They start at 0.5 and drift down. Low needs generate distress signals in the
hypothalamus, and hunger below 0.4 produces pain signals and an amygdala
response.

```js
brain.getNeeds();          // { hunger, energy, joy }
brain.setNeeds({ hunger: 0.2 });
brain.handleInteraction('feed', 1.0);  // reduces hunger, rewards
```

The body is a position in a unit square, plus heading, speed, and energy.

```js
brain.getBody(); // { x, y, heading, speed, energy }
```

`integrateWorldState()` reads the body and needs and turns them into neural
signals: spatial position relative to centre, distance from the border,
motion, and need pressure.

---

## Motor intent

The motor region is divided into four quadrants: right, left, down, up.

`getMotorIntent()` samples the mean activation of each quadrant and returns
the difference between opposing pairs.

```js
const intent = brain.getMotorIntent();
// { dx: -0.62, dy: 0.78, strength: 0.41 }
```

`dx` and `dy` are a normalized direction. `strength` is 0..1, scaled by how
much of the motor region is active.

The brain does not move itself — it expresses an intent, and your code
decides what to do with it. `brain.move(dx, dy, intensity)` applies the
intent to the brain's own body model and fires the corresponding motor and
cerebellar pulses.

---

## Reafference

Reafference is the brain noticing its own activity — the "correlate of
action". Here it means: which association neurons are currently firing.

```js
const reaf = brain.reafference(20);
reaf.indices;  // the top N association neuron indices
reaf.strength; // 0..1, how far they deviate from baseline
```

It is computed by comparing current association potentials against a slow
moving baseline, then taking the largest deviations.

`MemoryCortex.recallByReafference()` uses this to bias recall: memories
whose encoding pattern overlaps with currently-firing neurons come first.

```js
// Inside Brain.recall():
const reaf = this.core.reafference(20);
const nodes = this.memory.recallByReafference(reaf.indices, query, emotion, topN, context);
```

---

## Memory

A memory node holds `content`, `entities`, `emotion`, `salience`,
`dopamine`, `timestamp`, `accessCount`, `type`, and `turnId`.

Four types, decaying at different rates:

| Type | Decay | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `episodic` | Fastest (1.8x) | Things that happened. |
| `semantic` | Slowest (0.6x) | Facts. |
| `procedural` | Medium | How to do something. |
| `utterance` | Very slow | Speech. What `hear()` stores. |

Recall is a blend of three factors:

1. **Entity overlap** — how many of the query's entities the memory has.
2. **Emotion match** — whether the emotional tone matches.
3. **Reafference** — whether the neural encoding overlaps with what is
   firing now.

Salience and recency then affect the ordering.

Decay only happens when you call `brain.forget()`.

---

## Concepts

A concept is a label on an experienced cluster.

```js
brain.learn('ember', { bright: 0.9, hot: 0.8 }, { valence: 0.4 }, 'watch', 0.6);
```

The concept accumulates:

- **Sensory features** — a weighted map of feature names to values.
- **Emotion** — `{ valence, arousal, approach }`, averaged over learnings.
- **Activation** — how strongly it is currently lit.
- **Associations** — links to other concepts.

Activation decays over time and is boosted when the word is heard or
recalled. `activeConcepts()` returns the strongest ones.

`netEmotion()` sums the emotion of all active concepts, which is how a
character's overall mood shifts toward whatever it has been thinking about.

---

## Beliefs

Beliefs are claims with provenance, kept deliberately separate from memories.

```js
brain.believe({
  topic: 'fire',
  claim: 'fire is warm',
  source: 'observation',
  confidence: 0.8,
  verified: true,
});
```

Keeping the roles separate prevents a generated sentence or a repeated
thought from silently becoming knowledge.

`deliberate()` clusters claims whose text overlaps by token similarity
(threshold 0.55), then decides whether to conclude:

- **Concluded** if the leading cluster is verified, or has 2+ independent
  sources and confidence >= 0.45.
- **Not concluded** otherwise.

The store caps at 500 beliefs, evicting the weakest (unverified, low
confidence, oldest) first.

---

## Metacognition and homeostasis

### Metacognition

Predicts the next internal state before you respond, then scores itself
after.

```js
const record = brain.predict({ intent: 'question', emotion: 'happy' }, 0.6);
// ... generate a response ...
const delta = brain.observe(record, 'because fire is warm?');
```

The prediction is a function of emotion, novelty (from reafference), arousal,
and drive. The observation compares what was predicted against what actually
happened, and produces an accuracy score.

The error is fed back as dopamine through `brain.reward()` / `brain.punish()`.

The cue weights adapt. A missed valence prediction raises `emotion_cue`; an
accurate prediction decays all weights slightly. The log keeps the last 20
records.

### Homeostasis

Watches a rolling window of 20 turns and looks for the metric that is
furthest outside its target range.

| Metric | Target |
| --- | --- |
| `prediction_accuracy` | 0.55 to 1.0 |
| `interrupt_rate` | 0.0 to 0.3 |
| `memory_usefulness` | 0.3 to 1.0 |
| `goal_resolution_rate` | 0.4 to 1.0 |

When it finds a problem, it proposes **one** small mutation to a genome
parameter, runs a 10-turn trial, and then accepts the change (if it improved
by at least 0.02 and did not degrade anything else by more than 0.05) or
reverts it.

Every trial is written to the ledger, which you can read:

```js
brain.homeostasis.ledger;
brain.homeostasis.ledgerSummary(3);
```

---

## Growth

Neurogenesis adds neurons over time.

**Distribution.** New neurons are apportioned across the 16 regions by
`base size × growth weight`. The default weights favour the plastic
regions:

| Region | Weight |
| --- | --- |
| `hippocampus` | 3.0 |
| `association` | 2.6 |
| `prefrontal` | 2.2 |
| `temporal` | 1.6 |
| `sensory` | 1.4 |
| `visual`, `acc` | 1.2 |
| `basalGanglia`, `motor`, `cerebellum` | 1.0 |
| `thalamus` | 0.8 |
| `amygdala` | 0.7 |
| `hypothalamus` | 0.4 |
| `vta` | 0.3 |
| `locusCoeruleus`, `raphe` | 0.2 |

You can override any of these with `growthProfile`.

**Wiring.** Each newborn neuron gets:

- `growthFanout` (default 8) local recurrent connections in both directions,
  with weights in 0.1 to 0.5.
- `growthFanout` connections for each long-range projection the region
  participates in, using that rule's weight range.

So a grown region keeps its role in the circuit.

**Preservation.** The brain is remapped, not rebuilt. Potentials, thresholds,
decay rates, inhibitory flags, and learned synapse weights all survive, with
synapse targets rewritten through the remap table.

**Cadence.** `tick()` calls `maybeGrow()`, which adds a batch if
`growthInterval` ticks have passed since the last event. Setting
`growthInterval: 0` disables automatic growth entirely.
